question: Socrates' jury is usually put at 500; he said 30 votes going the other way would have acquitted him. How many voted guilty?
move: A vote that changes sides counts twice: once lost, once gained.
trap: Reading 30 switched votes as a 30-vote margin, not a 60-vote one.
hint: A switched vote leaves one pile and joins the other; in Athens a tie meant acquittal.
steps: Switching 30 votes takes 30 from guilty and adds 30 to not guilty.
A tie acquitted, so after the switch guilty would stand at exactly 250 of 500.
reference: Plato, Apology 36a, trans. Grube, in Plato: Complete Works, ed. Cooper, Hackett, 1997
